BPR-max uses negative-only weights s=softmax(r_neg) and loss −log Σj[sj·sigmoid(r_pos−rj)] + λΣj[sj·rj²]. The logarithm surrounds the weighted sum; averaging weighted log-sigmoids implements a different objective. Regularization penalizes negative scores, not embeddings or score differences. Gradients flow through the softmax weights in both terms; do not detach them. The official implementation optionally applies ELU before computing these quantities and adds 1e−24 inside the logarithm. [Paper, Eq.16](https://www.encompass-project.eu/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/recurrentNN.pdf), [official PyTorch code](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py).

Official sampling combines other minibatch targets with additional draws, shared across rows, drawn with replacement with probability proportional to training frequency^sample_alpha. It neither deduplicates nor rejects previously seen items or target collisions. Only each row’s designated positive diagonal column is masked; another column containing that same item remains a negative. Consequently, an item repeated m times receives aggregate softmax mass proportional to m·exp(r), affecting ranking and regularization; removing duplicates changes the objective unless multiplicity is retained. Excluding padding, positive IDs or history items in a padded-history adapter is an explicit departure from native sampling. [Official sampler and loss](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py).

For 32 negatives per valid position, a stable PyTorch adaptation is logw=log_softmax(neg.float(),−1), ranking=−logsumexp(logw+F.logsigmoid(pos.float()−neg.float()),−1), plus λΣexp(logw)·neg². This omits the official epsilon floor. Reduce over valid positions only; ensure every row has a valid negative. Use finite scores for regularization to avoid 0·∞ after masking. Vectorize GPU sampling and sampled-item scoring; avoid full-catalog logits and Python rejection loops. For N valid positions and dimension D, gathered embeddings require O(N·32·D) memory; chunk positions if necessary. [PyTorch logsumexp](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.logsumexp.html).
